case.case_title: Weerasinghe v. Premaratne, Police Sergeant and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. (F.R) Application No. 477/96, decided on 31 October 1997

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was illegally detained at the police station in violation of Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was arrested on 7.5.96 and detained illegally at the police station until 10.5.96 without being produced before a judge, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied arresting the petitioner on 7.5.96, claiming he was arrested only on 10.5.96 and challenged the petitioner's character.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested by police on 7.5.96 and detained at Pannala police station for over 24 hours.
Petitioner was produced before the Magistrate only on 10.5.96 at 5.30 pm and released on bail on 11.5.96.
Petitioner's family made repeated attempts to secure his release during detention.
Respondents claimed arrest occurred on 10.5.96, not 7.5.96.
Court found petitioner was indeed arrested on 7.5.96 and illegally detained until 10.5.96.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any detained person be brought before a judge and not held without legal order. The court emphasized the constitutional guarantee against illegal detention.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found credible evidence, including affidavits and contemporaneous letters, that the petitioner was arrested on 7.5.96 and detained without being produced before a judge until 10.5.96, violating Article 13(2). The respondents' denial and police records were found unreliable.
principles_established: Detention without being brought before a judge violates Article 13(2).
Police records may be unreliable in fundamental rights cases.
Contemporaneous documents and affidavits are important evidence in establishing detention dates.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner was illegally detained from 7.5.96 to 10.5.96 in violation of Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The court ordered compensation and costs to be paid to the petitioner by the respondents.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court's determination that the petitioner was unlawfully detained without being brought before a judge, which formed the basis for granting relief.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the petitioner was arrested on 7.5.96 and illegally kept in custody until 10.5.96 without being produced before a magistrate, violating Article 13(2).
